why: Same notions: B's levelTo f (m+l) m equals levelMap f m ∘ inclK m l (pointwise via toBase_inclK), B's membership hypothesis at l = 0 plus C¹ on U_m is IsSc0, and sc^{k+1} is IsSck (k+1); so A ⇒ B is proposition_1_19_text (the text's hypothesis, not the stronger C^{k+1}-on-every-level one) on the sc-domain U. B ⇒ A fails for a genuine reason: every conjunct of A is stated for an arbitrary IsScDomain U (open-in-convex levels with unique differentiability, e.g. a closed disc), while B covers only relatively open subsets of partial quadrants. Restricted to those domains all five conjuncts follow from B (rt_check OK): proposition_1_19_text and its sc-smooth version directly, proposition_1_19 and IsScSmooth.of_contDiffOn_levels because C^{k+1} on every level implies C^{l+1} on U_{m+l} → F_m, and proposition_1_19_zero with its named derivative family fderivWithin ℝ f U by uniqueness of derivatives on U₁ and density of E₁ in E₀. So the only gap is the domain class.
